t.2.99.1: Then to Bharata, who was speaking thus once again, the illustrious elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, highly honored in the midst of his kinsmen, made reply.
t.2.99.2: These words that you have spoken thus are fitting for a son born to Kaikeyī from Daśaratha, the best of kings.
t.2.99.3: Long ago, brother, when our father married your mother, he promised your maternal grandfather the kingdom as the supreme bride-price.
t.2.99.4: And in the battle between the gods and the asuras, the king, the lord of the earth, our master, greatly delighted and propitiated by her, granted a boon to your mother.
t.2.99.5: Then your illustrious mother, that lady of fair complexion, having first made him give his solemn promise, asked that best of men for two boons.
t.2.99.6: Kingship for you, O tiger among men, and likewise exile for me: that boon the king, bound by his word, granted to her just as she asked.
t.2.99.7: By that same father I too have been enjoined here, O bull among men, to dwell in the forest for fourteen years, a dwelling that stems from the granting of the boon.
t.2.99.8: So I, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa and by Sītā, have come to this uninhabited forest without resistance, abiding by my father's word of truth.
t.2.99.9: You too, simply by saying “So be it,” should make our father, the lord of kings, a speaker of truth through your swift consecration.
t.2.99.10: For my sake, O Bharata, free the king, our lord, from his debt; save our father, O knower of dharma, and gladden our mother.
t.2.99.11: For it is heard, dear one, that long ago a glorious saying was sung by Gaya as he performed sacrifice in the land of the Gayas itself, concerning the ancestors.
t.2.99.13: Many sons, virtuous and deeply learned, are to be wished for, so that of all of them gathered together, at least one might go to Gayā.
t.2.99.12: Because a son rescues his father from the hell named Put, he is therefore called putra, or else because the son protects his forefathers.
t.2.99.15: Go to Ayodhyā, O Bharata, and win the affection of the people; go, O hero, together with Śatrughna and with all the twice-born.
t.2.99.14: Thus all the royal sages have firmly believed, O son of a king. Therefore, O best of men, O lord, save your father from hell.
t.2.99.16: I too, without delay, shall enter the Daṇḍaka forest, O king, accompanied by these two, Vaidehī and Lakṣmaṇa.
t.2.99.17: Become yourself the king of men, O Bharata, and I too shall be the king of kings among the wild beasts of the forest. Go now, overjoyed, to the finest of cities, and I, rejoicing too, shall enter the Daṇḍaka forest.
t.2.99.18: Bharata, let the parasol that wards off the sun's glare cast its cool shade over your head; I too shall happily take refuge in that far finer shade of these forest trees.
t.2.99.19: Śatrughna, of sound judgment, is your companion, and Saumitri is known to be my foremost friend. We four excellent sons, O Bharata, shall keep the lord of men steadfast in truth; do not give way to despair.
